name: ML-PREPARE-TRAIN-1
hypothesis: Adding the 442 Prepare-menu decisions (action schema 2, 49 real PREPARE_CARD choices) to the training set lets Policy v2/v3 imitate the player on Prepare-menu decisions better than the same architecture trained only on the earlier schema-1 decisions, without lowering imitation quality on decisions without Prepare.
baseline: control group: identical architecture, seed, config and train/validation matches, restricted to action-schema-1 decisions (the data every earlier checkpoint could use); uniform random menu choice is the floor.
selection: minimum validation cross-entropy over the group's own validation rows (control: schema-1 rows only, so it never sees a Prepare menu)

verdict_rules.pooled_partitions: validation + test_seen (26 matches); paired differences = prepare group minus control, averaged over seeds; 95% interval from a 2000-draw bootstrap over whole matches (seed 20261015)
verdict_rules.P1: cross-entropy difference on Prepare-menu decisions < 0 and the 95% interval upper bound < 0
verdict_rules.P2: that difference is < 0 separately in validation and in test_seen, and in at least 2 of 3 seeds in each
verdict_rules.N1: no regression without Prepare: cross-entropy difference on no-Prepare-menu decisions has mean <= +0.03 and 95% upper bound <= +0.05
verdict_rules.N2: no over-recommendation: top-1 is a PREPARE_CARD action in Prepare-menu decisions at most 2x as often as the player chose Prepare there (pooled)
verdict_rules.PROMISING: P1, P2, N1 and N2 for the architecture; overall PROMISING needs both architectures
verdict_rules.REGRESSION: mean cross-entropy difference on no-Prepare-menu decisions >= +0.05 in both validation and test_seen, or top-1 Prepare rate > 3x the player's rate; overall REGRESSION if either architecture regresses
verdict_rules.note: None of the verdicts authorises a LIVE switch; it needs new independent matches.
